title: European Union increases NaturAfrica initiative funding to 1.6 billion euros
excerpt: Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera announced the funding boost at the COP17 biodiversity conference in Yerevan.
bodyHtml:
Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera announced on October 16, 2026, that the European Union has increased its contribution to the flagship NaturAfrica initiative to a total of 1.6 billion euros. This figure represents an increase of 200 million euros over the initial commitment for the project.

The additional funding is allocated to the Greater Zakouma landscape in Chad, Fouta Djallon in Guinea, and various transboundary landscapes located in the Congo Basin and southern Africa. Ribera stated that the European Union is on track to double its international biodiversity finance to 7 billion euros for the 2021–2027 period.

The European Union also announced the launch of a Group of Friends on Nature Credits at the conference. This initiative is intended to promote a sustainable finance taxonomy and strengthen international cooperation regarding high-integrity nature credits with strong safeguards and fair benefit-sharing with local communities.
topic: Speech by Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera at 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17)
